t: A Muslim dynasty of Arab origin that ruled Shirvan, in the north-east of modern Azerbaijan, from 861 to 1538.
It survived by accepting the overlordship of caliphs, Seljuks, Georgians, Mongols and Timurids in turn.
Its court patronised Khaqani and Nizami, and Khalilullah I built the Palace of the Shirvanshahs in Baku.
dyk: Nizami Ganjavi’s Layla and Majnun, one of the most retold love stories of the Islamic world, was composed in 1188 at the request of Shirvanshah Akhsitan I.
ev: Haytham ibn Khalid declares himself Shirvanshah
Nizami completes Layla and Majnun for Akhsitan I
The Mongols under Jebe and Subutai take Shamakhi
Ibrahim I founds the Derbendi line and revives the state
Khalilullah I completes the mosque of his palace in Baku
Farrukh Yasar kills Shaykh Haydar, father of the future Shah Ismail
Ismail I defeats and kills Farrukh Yasar at the Battle of Jabani
Tahmasp I annexes Shirvan to the Safavid Empire
